title: How Hormozi would take a roofing startup from $32K to $250K/month in 90 days
summary: Hormozi coaches a two-month-old roofing contractor by finding the highest-return motion (high-volume repairs), then layering a menu close, VSSLs, a maintenance membership and speed upcharges on a door-knocking engine. The business went from under $32K to about $250K in 90 days.

principles.text: Focus scarce time and money on the highest-return activity you can already do reliably.
principles.quote: I want to focus all efforts on the highest return stuff that you can do right now.

principles.text: Look for work other people cast aside, then systemize it so it earns strong gross profit at high volume.
principles.quote: I love when there it's like when when there's something that's been cast aside by other people, right? Like no one wants to do this particular thing, but then you orient a business in such a way that you can actually make really good gross profits on it.

principles.text: Use the menu close: unsell what they don't need, prescribe what they do, offer A or B, then card on file.
principles.quote: Step one is that Amanda's going to unsell what they don't need. >> Mhm. >> So, she gains trust.

principles.text: Sell speed: let customers pay to move to the front of the line. Same work, more margin.
principles.quote: If you're ever not sure how to add margin to a business, especially if you're supply constraint, meaning you have more people who want your stuff than you have the ability to do, add speed incentives for people to just move to the front of the line.

principles.text: Tack a maintenance membership onto the end of a service to turn one-time customers into recurring ones and raise LTV.
principles.quote: if you can tack that on the end, it takes the business from being one-time business to recurring business, which is obviously significantly more valuable and dramatically increases LTV.

principles.text: Make commissions concrete per action so reps know exactly how many doors equal how much money.
principles.quote: Want to go make 10 bucks? Knock that door. Want to make another 10 bucks? Knock that door.
